run.change_description: fix(utils/body,validator): normalize Content-Type media type for case-insensitive matching

summary.intent: Normalize the media-type portion of the Content-Type header before matching in parseBody() and validator('json'|'form'), so mixed/upper-case values like `Application/JSON` or `Application/X-WWW-Form-Urlencoded` are accepted the same as their canonical lowercase form, without altering case-sensitive parameters such as multipart boundaries.
summary.issue_fit: Full — parseBody() and validator('json'|'form') now match Content-Type media types case-insensitively while preserving parameter case (e.g. multipart boundaries), matching issue honojs/hono#5060's suggested fix and suggested tests.
summary.coverage: All 6 changed files (src/utils/body.ts, src/utils/body.test.ts, src/utils/buffer.ts, src/utils/buffer.test.ts, src/validator/validator.ts, src/validator/validator.test.ts) read in full diff and surrounding context, including HonoRequest's `bodyCache`/`#cachedBody` caching and validator.ts's pre-existing `bufferToFormData` usage that body.ts now shares. No must-fix or risk-area (security, data-loss, destructive-migration, released-compatibility) candidates surfaced, so no verification batch was required.

findings.title: Avoid buffering the whole body for every multipart/urlencoded parseBody() call
findings.trigger: Any `parseBody()` call whose Content-Type media type is `multipart/form-data` or `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, including the previously-working canonical-case requests that this fix did not need to touch.
findings.impact: `parseFormData` now always reads the full body into an `ArrayBuffer` and rebuilds a `Response` solely to call `.formData()` on a header-normalized copy, replacing the prior direct `request.formData()` call. Large uploads the platform could parse without fully materializing now pay a full in-memory buffering cost inside Hono on every request, not only the mixed-case ones this PR targets.
findings.change: Keep the previous `request.formData()` fast path when the media type is already exactly `multipart/form-data` or `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (normalization would be a no-op), and only fall back to the buffer-and-normalize path used here for non-canonical casing.

observations.fact: body.ts's `parseFormData` now delegates to `bufferToFormData` (src/utils/buffer.ts), the same helper validator.ts's `form` target already used before this PR, centralizing the media-type-case normalization in one place instead of duplicating it per call site.

This PR's body.test.ts diff also replaces a `vi.spyOn`-based mock of `formData()` in the file-object-properties preservation test with a real `FormData`, a test-hygiene cleanup bundled into the Content-Type fix rather than part of it.
observations.evidence: src/utils/body.test.ts diff, the file-object-properties preservation test.

requirements.evidence: src/utils/body.ts:100-105 now compares `contentType?.split(';')[0].trim().toLowerCase()` against the lowercase media types instead of case-sensitive `startsWith()`; src/validator/validator.ts:24-26 add the `/i` flag to `jsonRegex`/`multipartRegex`/`urlencodedRegex`. New passing tests in body.test.ts and validator.test.ts exercise `Application/JSON` and `Application/X-WWW-Form-Urlencoded`.

requirements.source: issue-5060/"Parameter values such as multipart boundaries should remain intact"
requirements.evidence: src/utils/buffer.ts:113 lowercases only the substring before the first `;` via `contentType.replace(/^[^;]+/, ...)`, leaving `boundary=sampleBoundary` untouched. buffer.test.ts's new 'keeping the boundary' case uses a mixed-case boundary value and passed when run.
6 new test cases added across body.test.ts, buffer.test.ts, and validator.test.ts covering mixed-case multipart, urlencoded, and JSON media types; all ran and passed at the reviewed head.
